[[Medford, NJ]] }} '''Jason Thompson''' (born [[July 21]], [[1986]]) is currently the starting center of the [[Rider University]] men's basketball team. Thompson led his [[Lenape High School]] squad to the 2004 New Jersey Group IV State Title.Carchidi, Sam. [http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=PI&s_site=philly&p_multi=PI&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0FE57C3CA77EAFD6&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM "Lenape's Thompson selects Rider"], ''[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]'', [[October 21]], [[2003]]. Accessed [{April 9]], [[2008]]. "Senior Jason Thompson, a 6-foot-8 forward/center from Lenape High, has made an oral commitment to attend Rider University on a basketball scholarship, Indians coach Bill Lange announced yesterday." He is projected to be drafted late in the first round or early in the second round of the upcoming [[2008 NBA Draft]] in the summer.[http://www.nbadraft.net NBADraft.net | Home] His hometown is [[Mount Laurel Township, New Jersey]]. Thompson is currently listed at 6 feet, 10 inches, and 245 lbs. He was one of three players in the [[NCAA]] in 2007 to average 20 points, and 10 rebounds per game. The other two individuals were [[Kevin Durant]] of the [[University of Texas]] and [[Nick Fazekas]] of the [[University of Nevada]]. As a senior during the 2007-2008 season, Thompson averaged 20.4 points per game, 12.1 rebounds per game, and a hefty 2.7 blocks per game. His strongest performance was on March 9, 2008 when he scored 32 points and grabbed 18 rebounds against [[Marist College]]. He led Rider to the 2008 [[Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference]] Tournament finale against [[Siena College]] falling short 74-53. Rider finished the regular season and conference tournament schedule with a strong 23-10 record, but still missed an at-large bid to the [[National Invitation Tournament]]. However, Rider did receive a bid to the inaugural [[College Basketball Invitational]] tournament in 2008. Rider lost its first round game to the [[Old Dominion University]] Monarchs 68-65. Thompson's younger brother, Ryan, also plays guard for the Rider Broncs, and will be a junior in the upcoming 2008-2009 season. Jason Thompson is arguably the best and most notable basketball player to come out of the Rider program since [[Digger Phelps]] graduated in 1963. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Thompson, Jason}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:1986 births]] [[Category:People from Burlington County, New Jersey]] [[Category:Rider University alumni]]
